q: The Great Bath of the Indus Valley Civilization was discovered at which site?
The Great Bath is a large brick-lined tank at Mohenjo-daro, suggesting ritual bathing. Tip: Great Bath = Mohenjo-daro, Dockyard = Lothal.
The Harappan script is best described as:
Harappan seals carry short inscriptions, but the script remains undeciphered. It is mostly pictographic with about 400-600 signs.
Which Harappan site is famous for its ancient dockyard?
Lothal in Gujarat had a tidal dockyard linked to the Gulf of Khambhat. It was a bead-making and trade centre.
Fire altars, suggesting ritual practices, were found at:
Kalibangan in Rajasthan yielded rows of fire altars and a ploughed field. Tip: Kalibangan = fire altars + ploughed field.
Mehrgarh is important because it provides evidence of:
Mehrgarh, in Balochistan, shows early wheat and barley farming and domesticated animals before the mature Harappan phase.
Which Harappan site is known for a large water reservoir and a signboard?
Dholavira in Gujarat has sophisticated water reservoirs and a ten-sign board. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The largest Harappan site located in India is:
Rakhigarhi, in Haryana, is the largest Harappan site in India. Mohenjo-daro and Harappa are in Pakistan.
The famous bronze figure of the Dancing Girl was found at:
The Dancing Girl is a bronze sculpture from Mohenjo-daro. It shows the Harappans' skill in metal casting.
Harappan seals were mostly made of which material?
Most Harappan seals are made of steatite, a soft stone that is easy to carve and then fired.
Burzahom, a Neolithic site with pit dwellings, is located in:
Burzahom is in the Kashmir Valley. Its early inhabitants lived in pits cut into the ground.
The Bhimbetka rock shelters, famous for prehistoric paintings, are in:
Bhimbetka lies in the Vindhyan hills of Madhya Pradesh and has paintings from the Palaeolithic to historic periods.
Which metal was NOT used by the Harappans?
The Harappans belonged to the Bronze Age; iron came into use in India later. Tip: Harappan = bronze, not iron.
Chanhudaro, in Sindh, was a craft centre famous for bead making and shell working.
Which crop was NOT commonly cultivated by the Harappans?
Harappans grew wheat, barley, peas and cotton. Sugarcane cultivation became common in later periods.
The meaning of the name Mohenjo-daro is:
Mohenjo-daro is Sindhi for mound of the dead. The site is in Sindh, Pakistan.
Which is the oldest of the four Vedas?
The Rigveda is the oldest Veda and contains hymns dedicated to various gods. The other three are later.
The Gayatri Mantra appears in which Veda?
The Gayatri Mantra is in the Rigveda and is dedicated to Savitri. Tip: Gayatri = Rigveda.
The Kalinga War, after which Ashoka embraced Buddhism, was fought in:
Ashoka fought the Kalinga War around 261 BCE. The bloodshed led him to adopt Dhamma and non-violence.
Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire around 321 BCE with the help of Chanakya.
Kautilya, also called Chanakya, wrote the Arthashastra on statecraft and economics.
Ashokan inscriptions were mainly written in which script in most of India?
Most Ashokan edicts use Prakrit in Brahmi script; in the northwest, Kharosthi was also used.
The Gupta period is often called the Golden Age of India because of advances in:
The Guptas patronised literature, astronomy, mathematics and temple art; Kalidasa and Aryabhata belong to this era.
Who is called the Napoleon of India by historian V. A. Smith?
Samudragupta's extensive military campaigns earned him the title Napoleon of India in V. A. Smith's writing.
The four Vedas are Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and:
The Atharvaveda is the fourth Veda and contains spells, charms and philosophical hymns.
In the Vedic period, the assembly of elders was called:
Sabha and Samiti were important assemblies in the early Vedic period. Sabha was the assembly of elders.
Dharmamahamatra, an officer appointed by Ashoka, was responsible for:
Dharmamahamatra looked after welfare, religious harmony and the propagation of Dhamma.
The iron pillar at Mehrauli, Delhi, is associated with which ruler?
The rust-resistant iron pillar at Mehrauli is linked to Chandragupta II of the Gupta dynasty.
Nalanda Mahavihara was founded during the reign of:
Nalanda was founded under Kumaragupta I and became a major Buddhist learning centre.
Buddha delivered his first sermon at:
The first sermon, the Dhammachakkapavattana Sutta, was delivered at Sarnath near Varanasi.
Ashoka sent his daughter Sanghamitra to spread Buddhism in:
Sanghamitra and her brother Mahendra are credited with spreading Buddhism in Sri Lanka.
The First Battle of Panipat in 1526 was fought between Babur and:
Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in 1526, establishing the Mughal Empire. He used gunpowder and artillery effectively.
The construction of the Qutub Minar was started by:
Qutb-ud-din Aibak began the Qutub Minar; it was completed by his successor Iltutmish.
Which Delhi Sultanate ruler introduced strict market regulations and price controls?
Alauddin Khalji controlled markets, prices and the supply of goods to keep his army and city stable.
Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to:
He moved the capital to Daulatabad in the Deccan, but the experiment failed and the capital returned to Delhi.
The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by:
Harihara and Bukka founded Vijayanagara in 1336. The city was on the Tungabhadra river.
Krishnadevaraya, the Vijayanagara ruler, wrote which work in Telugu?
Krishnadevaraya wrote Amuktamalyada, a Telugu poetic work on the life of Andal.
Akbar promulgated Din-i-Ilahi in 1582 as a syncretic faith. It attracted very few followers.
The Battle of Talikota in 1565 led to the decline of:
A coalition of Deccan sultanates defeated Vijayanagara at Talikota, leading to its decline.
Sher Shah Suri is credited with introducing the silver coin called:
Sher Shah Suri introduced the rupiya, a silver coin that influenced later Indian currency.
The chief architect of the Taj Mahal was:
Ustad Ahmad Lahauri is generally credited as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal.
Baburnama was originally written in which language?
Babur wrote his memoirs in Chagatai Turkish; they were later translated into Persian.
Who was the first woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate?
Razia Sultan ruled from 1236 to 1240 and was the first woman to rule Delhi.
The Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 was fought between the Marathas and:
Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas at Panipat in 1761, checking Maratha expansion in the north.
The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of:
Ibn Battuta came to India in the 14th century and served as a judge under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674 at:
Shivaji's coronation took place at Raigad fort in 1674, marking the rise of Maratha power.
Who founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828?
Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj and campaigned against sati and for women's education.
The Arya Samaj was founded by:
Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 and gave the slogan Back to the Vedas.
Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in:
Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 at Belur, focused on service and education.
The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by:
A. O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, played a key role in founding the INC. W. C. Bonnerjee was its first president.
The Partition of Bengal was announced in 1905 by:
Viceroy Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal in 1905, triggering the Swadeshi movement.
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in:
On 13 April 1919, General Dyer ordered firing on an unarmed crowd at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar.
Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in:
The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920 and was withdrawn after the Chauri Chaura incident in 1922.
The Dandi March of 1930 was a protest against:
Gandhi marched from Sabarmati to Dandi to make salt and defy the British salt monopoly.
The Quit India Movement was launched in:
Gandhi gave the call Do or Die in August 1942. The movement demanded an immediate end to British rule.
Who led the Indian National Army (INA) during the freedom struggle?
Subhas Chandra Bose reorganised the INA and gave the slogan Give me blood and I will give you freedom.
The Rowlatt Act of 1919 was opposed because it allowed:
The Rowlatt Act allowed imprisonment without trial, leading to nationwide protests and the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy.
The Simon Commission was boycotted because:
The all-British Simon Commission arrived in 1928; Indians protested the absence of Indian representation.
The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed between Gandhi and:
The Poona Pact replaced separate electorates for Dalits with reserved seats in joint electorates.
Who was the first woman president of the Indian National Congress?
Annie Besant was elected INC president in 1917. Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman president.
Mangal Pandey is associated with the Revolt of:
Mangal Pandey attacked British officers at Barrackpore in 1857, a spark for the revolt.
The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament in:
The Indian Independence Act 1947 created India and Pakistan as independent dominions.
The Constitution of India was adopted on:
The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949; it came into force on 26 January 1950.
Who was the first President of India?
Dr Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India (1950-1962).
The States Reorganisation Act, based on language, was passed in:
The States Reorganisation Act 1956 reorganised states largely on linguistic lines.
Goa was liberated from Portuguese rule in:
Operation Vijay in 1961 integrated Goa, Daman and Diu with India.
The Green Revolution in India is associated with:
M. S. Swaminathan led the Green Revolution, which used high-yielding wheat varieties and modern inputs.
The White Revolution, or Operation Flood, was led by:
Verghese Kurien led Operation Flood, which transformed India's dairy sector through cooperatives.
The Emergency in India was imposed in:
A national emergency was declared in June 1975 and lasted until March 1977.
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment is often called the:
The 42nd Amendment (1976) added socialist, secular and integrity to the Preamble and made many changes.
Panchayati Raj was given constitutional status by the:
The 73rd Amendment 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions; the 74th covers urban bodies.
In 1991, Finance Minister Manmohan Singh introduced reforms that opened the economy and reduced licensing.
India's first general election was held in:
The first general election took place between October 1951 and February 1952.
Sikkim became a state of India in:
Sikkim became the 22nd state of India in 1975 after a referendum abolished the monarchy.
The First Amendment to the Constitution was passed in:
The First Amendment 1951 added the Ninth Schedule and placed restrictions on free speech.
India's first National Emergency was declared in 1962 during the war with:
A national emergency was declared in 1962 during the India-China war, the first of three such emergencies.
